item.title: Gold Holds Steady as Progress on Hormuz Trims Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold traded in a narrow range, as the prospect of an interim deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz eased inflation concerns and reduced the odds of the US Federal Reserve raising interest rates.

item.title: Australia to Cut Price of Rooftop Solar for Factories, AFR Says
item.description: Australia will cut the price of installing solar panels on warehouse and factory rooftops, the Australian Financial Review reported, in the latest move by the government to accelerate the rollout of green energy.

item.title: Japan’s Nominal Wages Rise Again, Backing BOJ Rate Hike Case
item.description: Japanese wage growth remained firm on the back of solid corporate earnings and a tight labor market, bolstering the case for another Bank of Japan interest rate hike in coming months.

item.title: SoftBank Earnings to Test Appetite for AI Bets Beyond ChatGPT
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp.’s stock faces a critical test this week as investors seek reassurance that the company’s AI value extends beyond its debt-fueled bet on embattled ChatGPT operator OpenAI.

item.title: Lab Monkeys for $26,000 Show China’s Biotech Quest to Rival US
item.description: Prices of lab monkeys in China have surged, complicating new drug development trials and increasing the need for primate imports from neighboring countries.

item.title: New Zealand Unemployment Reaches 11-Year High on Fuel Shock
item.description: New Zealand’s jobless rate rose to an 11-year high in the second quarter as the global energy shock squeezed company profits while more people sought work.

item.title: Coupang’s Losses Grow After Fallout From Data Breach Deepens
item.description: Coupang Inc. reported a larger-than-expected loss, underscoring the damage from a massive personal data leak that resulted in heavy administrative fines in South Korea, its primary market.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set to Advance, Oil Drops on Iran: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to track Wall Street higher after optimism over a possible interim deal between Washington and Tehran eased concerns about energy supplies, lifting the S&P 500 Index to a record close. Oil fell and bonds gained.

item.title: Booking Holdings Keeps Full-Year Outlook on Resilient Travel
item.description: Booking Holdings Inc. maintained its full-year outlook for gross bookings and revenue due to resilient travel demand even as the Middle East conflict weighs on flight prices and capacity.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 5
item.description: Oil held a two-day drop on optimism a deal can be reached that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic AI Models Involved in More Security Incidents
item.description: Artificial intelligence models from OpenAI and Anthropic were involved in previously unreported cybersecurity incidents, marking the latest in a recent string of these events.

item.title: Whale Rock Sank 22% as AI Selloff Crippled Hedge Fund Returns
item.description: Whale Rock Capital Management’s flagship hedge fund is one of the biggest losers in last month’s AI selloff, with a 21.7% drop in July erasing about half of its gains for the year.

item.title: Compass Shares Jump on Cost Savings, Transaction Growth
item.description: Compass Inc. shares jumped as much as 15% in post-market trading after the real estate services firm said cost savings from the acquisition of competitor Anywhere were progressing ahead of schedule.

item.title: Wynn’s New Middle Eastern Resort to Open in September 2027
item.description: Wynn Resorts Ltd. said its first casino located in the Middle East will now open in September of next year.

item.title: Apollo Invests $1 Billion in Joint Venture With Starwood REIT
item.description: Apollo Global Management Inc. is investing $1.02 billion in a joint venture with Starwood Real Estate Income Trust, a commercial property vehicle known as SREIT that has struggled to provide liquidity to investors.

item.title: Japan Human-Sized Refrigerator Cooling Booth Sees Demand as Heat Waves Intensify
item.description: The glass door closes, and a curtain of cool air spills over your head, neck and shoulders, delivering instant relief from the punishing summer heat.

item.title: Prudential Tops Estimates as Revenue From Asset Manager Soars
item.description: Prudential Financial Inc. reported second-quarter results that beat Wall Street estimates as revenue from its asset manager surged.

item.title: Pipeline Owners Race to Build Capacity as AI Power Demand Jumps
item.description: US pipeline operators are racing to expand their capacity to help power new data centers.

item.title: US Revokes Brazilian Ambassador’s Visa Amid Diplomatic Spat
item.description: The Trump administration revoked the visa for Brazil’s ambassador to the US after the country delayed giving diplomatic approval to Washington’s choice for envoy to Brasilia, a senior State Department official said Tuesday.

item.title: Situational Awareness Not Target of Predatory Shorts, S3 Says
item.description: The losses that forced hedge fund Situational Awareness to sell stocks at deep discounts appear to be the result of highly concentrated positions in crowded trades, rather than a concerted effort by short-sellers, according to the founder of a company that analyzes short positioning data.

item.title: AMD Sales Outlook Disappoints Investors After AI-Fueled Rally
item.description: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. disappointed investors with its latest sales outlook, a sign shareholders expected more of a return from the global expansion of AI data centers.

item.title: Pinterest Revenue Outlook Disappoints Investors; Shares Slide
item.description: Pinterest Inc. gave a revenue outlook for the current quarter that disappointed investors worried about the company’s momentum despite posting strong user and revenue growth for the prior period.

item.title: Tanger Sees Boost from World Cup, Back to School Shoppers
item.description: Tanger Inc. boosted its outlook for a second time this year, as stronger domestic travel and early back-to-school shoppers have boosted traffic and sales at the real estate investment trust’s shopping centers.

item.title: Match’s Quarterly Revenue, Outlook Fall Shy of Analyst Estimates
item.description: Match Group Inc. gave a revenue forecast for the current quarter that narrowly missed analysts’ estimates, suggesting its dating sites still need to attract more younger users as part of its turnaround effort.

item.title: USD And JPY: Trump, Bessent Intervene to Rescue a Weakening Japanese Yen
item.description: One of the most dramatic foreign exchange market interventions in decades aims to stabilize the slumping yen — and stave off a larger crisis.

item.title: EchoStar’s Hughes Wins Approval to Use Lender Cash in Bankruptcy
item.description: A judge has allowed Hughes Satellite Systems Corp. to use noteholders’ cash to keep operating for the next four weeks, after a two-day court fight over how the company will pay its bills while in bankruptcy.

item.title: Cerberus Seeks $4 Billion for Second Supply Chain Fund
item.description: Cerberus Capital Management, co-founded by Deputy Secretary of Defense Stephen Feinberg, is looking to raise at least $4 billion for its latest supply-chain fund that backs investments critical to the US economy.

item.title: Samsung Reveals New 3D-Memory Roadmap in Bid for AI Tech Lead
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. offered a glimpse of its most advanced memory hardware, touting improved performance and power efficiency in a bid to overtake rivals SK Hynix Inc. and Micron Technology Inc. in the race for long-term dominance.

item.title: Thousands Seek NYC Pied-a-Terre Tax Relief, City Hall Says
item.description: Roughly 2,000 people have completed applications seeking an exemption from New York City’s newly-implemented pied-à-terre tax, a spokesperson for the Department of Finance said Tuesday.

item.title: Data Centers Exposed US Telecoms to China Hacks, US Panel to Say
item.description: US telecommunications companies connected their systems to data centers and related infrastructure in a way that exposed them to cybersecurity vulnerabilities, potentially opening the door to the massive Salt Typhoon hacking campaign that breached several mobile carriers two years ago, according to an upcoming House committee’s report.
